Standards, data, and talent are indispensable elements for fostering a healthy climate finance ecosystem, and their development relies on efforts and collaboration across different sectors. To this end, the HKMA primarily collaborates with other relevant government departments, regulators, academic institutions, and the financial industry through the Steering Group to advance these elements. In addition to the development of the local green taxonomy framework mentioned above, the Steering Group has promoted industry skills training and improved Hong Kong's data resources through its established "Green and Sustainable Finance Centre." Furthermore, the Steering Group has made good progress in other areas, including mandatory disclosure of climate-related information and opportunities in carbon markets. In 2022, the HKMA further strengthened the Exchange Fund's work on responsible investment, notably setting a target for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. Concurrently, we have optimized risk management to enhance the Exchange Fund's climate resilience and risk-adjusted long-term returns. Additionally, to fully capitalize on opportunities that climate change may present, we are committed to promoting sustainable investments by the Exchange Fund, seeking opportunities that support climate transition and mitigation to enhance the portfolio's long-term returns. By the end of 2021, the weighted average carbon intensity of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio had decreased by 43% compared to 2017 levels. In fact, the Exchange Fund's risk exposure to high-carbon assets has consistently remained lower than that of the overall market. Going forward, we will continue to advance toward the net-zero target by continuously integrating environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into investment management processes, actively exercising asset ownership, maintaining collaboration with various stakeholders, and focusing on decarbonization and transition within the portfolio. At the HKMA, the "Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee," chaired by me, is responsible for formulating the HKMA's sustainability strategy. Our strategic direction is built upon three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Environmentally, we are committed to promoting a green workplace and advocating for a more environmentally friendly market to the public; regarding employees, as a responsible and caring employer, we actively foster a healthy and inclusive work environment; and in terms of social responsibility, we are dedicated to enhancing public financial literacy, promoting financial inclusion, and actively giving back to society. Compared to the levels when we began tracking our carbon footprint in 2015, our per capita greenhouse gas emissions, energy consumption, and paper usage in 2022 all achieved double-digit reductions. More importantly, we have developed a roadmap to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In the short term, our goal is to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions and reduce Scope 2 emissions by 63% by 2030 or earlier, using 2015 as the baseline. Addressing climate change and promoting sustainable development require continuous efforts and collaboration from all parties. On this critical global issue, we understand the necessity of leading by example and working together with like-minded peers and international organizations. The next section will outline the HKMA's short-term plans and key work priorities in addressing climate change under its core functions. Achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier is a formidable task, and we will spare no effort to achieve this goal. We are confident that, through the joint efforts of all our colleagues, the financial industry, and the general public, we can successfully meet future climate challenges.  Chief Executive, Eddie Yue

In 2023, the HKMA will continue to promote sustainable development within Hong Kong's financial sector and fulfill its responsibilities as a responsible investor and sustainable institution. At the same time, through participation in international and regional organizations, the HKMA will also endeavor to promote the broad development and best practices of green and sustainable finance. As the banking regulator, we are committed to enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and further improving our green finance ecosystem to support banks' green transformation. Specifically, the HKMA will engage with banks to understand their progress in implementing regulatory requirements on climate risk management, incorporate climate factors into our supervisory review processes, and revise the banking sector's "Green Benchmark" common assessment framework. At the same time, the HKMA will support banks' efforts to enhance their climate resilience and risk management capabilities, for example by exploring various measures and technological solutions to assist banks in identifying, quantifying, and monitoring their climate risk exposures. The HKMA will also collaborate with banks to conduct the next round of climate risk stress tests as part of the regulator-led periodic stress testing for the 2023-2024 period. Participating banks will be required to assess their capacity to respond to climate risks based on an optimized stress testing framework that covers multiple stress scenarios, including extreme climate events and adverse economic conditions. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will closely monitor local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain communication with the industry to provide timely guidance on sales processes. We will also conduct off-site thematic assessments to gain a comprehensive understanding of the green and sustainable investment products offered by banks. Meanwhile, to strengthen the construction of a green finance ecosystem to support the green transformation of the financial industry, the HKMA is planning to consult the industry on the structure and core elements of establishing a local green taxonomy framework. In terms of market development, to promote Hong Kong as a regional hub for green and sustainable finance, the HKMA will assist the government in expanding the issuance scale of green bonds under the "Government Green Bond Scheme" and broaden the scheme's scope to cover sustainability bonds; at the same time, through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme," attract more green financing activities to be conducted in Hong Kong. The HKMA will also assist in implementing the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. In addition, the HKMA will continue to encourage more mainland local governments, institutions, and enterprises to conduct green financing through Hong Kong, and explore the feasibility of integrating green finance with technology. On the other hand, we will continue to collaborate with other government departments through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Bureau Steering Committee" on cross-industry issues such as skills training and data, green taxonomies, climate-related disclosures and sustainability reporting, and carbon market opportunities. Through the Green Banking Alliance, the HKMA will jointly launch various specialized programs with the International Finance Corporation in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps to make green finance a core business. Looking ahead, the Alliance will work closely with its founding members, global partners, and knowledge partners to launch a membership program to expand the Alliance's influence in the Asia region. At the same time, the Alliance will also strengthen the enhancement of professionals' capabilities within the industry, facilitate the sharing of green finance knowledge, and lead the launch of project initiatives in new areas. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, as a commitment to its participation in global climate action and the implementation of recommendations from the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures. Looking ahead, the HKMA will continue to integrate environmental, social, and governance factors into its investment management processes, strive to advance towards the net-zero emissions target, and fully support global climate action. As a responsible and sustainable institution, the HKMA cares not only about its employees but also about the general public and the surrounding environment. We have formulated a sustainability roadmap and established climate targets for our own operations as a commitment to our participation in global carbon reduction and climate action. The HKMA will continue to prioritize carbon emission reduction and encourage full support from employees to save energy and reduce waste. In addition, we will provide further guidance to employees to incorporate sustainability principles into procurement processes. To practice digital transformation and enhance operational flexibility, the HKMA will explore methods to modernize internal systems and applications to further improve work efficiency, while minimizing potential risks that may arise during the digital transformation process as much as possible.

Climate change represents a significant risk to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impacts of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations. To continue fulfilling their vital role in the financial system and to channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA also supports banks in enhancing their capabilities to detect environmental crimes and has participated in the recently released Hong Kong Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment, which covers areas such as environmental crimes and illegal wildlife trafficking. In 2022, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS)1 issued the Principles for the Effective Management and Supervision of Climate-Related Financial Risks and provided responses to frequently asked questions to clarify how the existing Basel framework addresses these risks. In light of these international developments, the HKMA will continue to commit to integrating climate-related factors into its regulatory framework. Following the issuance of Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Regulatory Policy Handbook in 2021, the HKMA has maintained communication with banks to exchange views on expectations, progress, and challenges in implementing the relevant regulatory requirements. To further strengthen the supervision of banks' climate risk management, the HKMA has formulated a two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, which was communicated to the banking industry in June. As part of the implementation of this two-year plan, the HKMA issued the revised Module SA-1 "Risk-Based Supervision" of the Regulatory Policy Handbook, enhancing the CAMEL2 rating system by incorporating climate risks into the risk-based supervisory process. Meanwhile, drawing on experience gained from the 2021 pilot programme, the HKMA has improved the scenarios and assessment framework for climate risk stress testing. The HKMA has also developed a plan to incorporate the next round of climate risk stress testing into the regulator-led periodic stress testing regime, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of the banking sector's resilience under extreme climate scenarios. Under this two-year plan, the HKMA is also strengthening its Green Assessment Framework for banks to reflect the latest developments in sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management and transition planning. At the same time, the HKMA is reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, aiming to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address risks related to climate change and the transition to net zero. Given the growing prevalence of banks issuing green and sustainable products, the HKMA conducted a thematic review primarily examining banks' development and ongoing management of these products. During the thematic review, the HKMA identified several good practices and issued a circular in December to share them with the industry, thereby enabling banks to progressively enhance their climate risk management capabilities. The application of technology can improve data availability and strengthen banks' capacity to manage climate risks. The HKMA has commenced the development of a common platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on real estate. Additionally, together with other central banks and regulators, the HKMA has completed a project under the Bank for International Settlements' Innovation Hub to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. The HKMA also attaches great importance to promoting sustainable and globally leading anti-money laundering practices; work in this area employs advanced analytics and regulatory technology, supported by fully automated regulatory data collection. Over the past 12 months, the HKMA has streamlined the anti-money laundering regulatory data collection process to reduce the manpower burden and paper usage for banks. To enhance transparency across financial markets and ensure greater consistency in green finance policies, the HKMA has collaborated with other financial regulators to establish a local green taxonomy framework. Generally referred to as a green taxonomy, this framework classifies economic activities as green or sustainable, providing a reference for authorities and market participants to determine whether a specific activity or its related products are genuinely green or sustainable. To this end, the HKMA has maintained engagement with the industry and other relevant stakeholders to explore the features and challenges of the framework in depth, and is preparing to propose and consult on the framework's structure and core elements in the first half of 2023. Recognizing that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various Financial Stability Reports. Through active participation in the Scenarios Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped to further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and the financial system. In terms of research, the HKMA conducted multiple applied research projects in 2022, delving into two major topics: greenwashing in the corporate green bond market3 and the role of disclosure in mitigating climate risk exposure4. The results of these studies assist in formulating policies and regulatory measures to address the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Internationally, the HKMA has shared research findings with a wide range of stakeholders through various channels, including international central bank research seminars and the Authority's Semi-Annual Report on Currency and Financial Stability. The HKMA's "Liquidity Arrangement Framework" is a collateralised standby liquidity facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA is studying the inclusion of sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, the HKMA helps foster policy dialogue at the international and regional levels on addressing climate change and its impacts on financial stability, drawing insights to enhance Hong Kong's financial system's climate resilience.

To consolidate Hong Kong's status as the regional hub for green and sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has intensified its efforts to enhance market awareness and engagement, provide necessary infrastructure and drivers, and support international initiatives to align with global standards. The Cross-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategy. The Steering Group's work is primarily guided by its Strategic Plan, which outlines six key focus areas and five action agendas to strengthen Hong Kong's financial ecosystem and build a greener and more sustainable future (Figure 1). These include: strengthening climate-related financial risk management to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a global risk management centre; promoting the flow of climate-related information across all levels to facilitate risk management, capital allocation, and investor protection; enhancing relevant skills among industry professionals and raising public awareness and understanding; encouraging product innovation and research measures to channel capital towards green and sustainable projects; seizing business opportunities from Mainland China to develop Hong Kong as the green finance centre for the Greater Bay Area (GBA); and strengthening regional and international cooperation. Actions taken thus far to advance sustainable finance in Hong Kong: Since its establishment, the Steering Group has made good progress. Its current work priorities include skills training and data collection under the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre (see below), the Green Taxonomy (see "Establishing a Green Taxonomy Framework to Facilitate Green Capital Flow" in Chapter 9, "Building a Sustainable Financial System"), climate-related disclosure and sustainability reporting, and carbon market opportunities. Specifically, in March, the Steering Group published a preliminary feasibility assessment of carbon market opportunities in Hong Kong and will support Hong Kong's development as a regional carbon trading centre, including the development of an international high-quality voluntary carbon market and seizing opportunities arising from GBA cooperation. In December, the Steering Group announced a collaboration with CDP to enhance data availability in Hong Kong and strengthen sustainability reporting. As part of this collaboration, the two parties developed a climate and environmental risk questionnaire targeting non-listed companies and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), facilitating companies' sustainability reporting and assisting financial institutions in collecting and analysing company-level data for risk assessment and related business decisions. This represents an important step by the Steering Group in expanding the scope of its data work to include SMEs, a previously less accessible yet vital segment of the economy. The Steering Group established the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre in July 2021 to coordinate training and policy formulation efforts among financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and academic institutions, and to build resources and databases. In the first half of 2022, the Centre launched three repositories focusing on data, training information, and internship opportunities, assisting the financial sector and other sectors in accessing data and learning resources related to green and sustainable finance. The resource repository provides data sources for assessing Hong Kong's physical risks. To assist in industry talent development, the Centre assisted the Government in launching the "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" in December, providing subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates participating in green and sustainable finance-related training and skills enhancement. Other measures promoting skills training include the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Scheme" to create more internship opportunities for students, and the development of a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the HKMA's "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" for banking practitioners. The "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme": The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the HKMA launched the "Green Banking Alliance," bringing together regional financial institutions, banking industry organisations, research institutes, and fintech providers to jointly develop a collaborative platform for green commercial banking. The Alliance aims to enable commercial banks and other financial institutions to fully realise their potential in making green finance a mainstream core business and to promote the financial sector's participation in global climate change-related activities. Its mode of operation includes providing a one-stop mutual learning platform for financial institutions to acquire the knowledge, tools, and information needed to formulate their own green finance roadmaps and transform into credible green financial institutions; gathering green finance leaders to connect green financial institutions across different emerging markets; promoting communication and exploring frontier issues; and advancing the global green finance agenda to unlock endless green and climate-related investment opportunities. In June, five global leading financial institutions became cornerstone members of the Alliance and are working closely with the IFC and the HKMA to encourage clients to adopt green strategies, promote best practices in green products and services, and unlock new business opportunities, contributing to the green economic transition. Additionally, three global partners and one knowledge partner committed in 2022 to providing climate expertise in areas such as innovation, standardisation, and academic research. Details of the Alliance and its membership structure are available on the relevant webpage (English version): Cornerstone Members; IFC and HKMA signed a Memorandum of Understanding. On the other hand, since March 2021, the Alliance has held 18 training sessions and roundtable discussions, attracting over 6,000 participants from across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. Furthermore, in June 2022, the Alliance, together with the Hong Kong Centre for Monetary and Financial Studies (the Centre), published its first frontier issue research report titled "Climate Risk: Definition, Measurement, Current Practices and Regulation." The HKMA has consistently promoted the issuance of green and sustainable debt and cultivated a local ecosystem for related professional services. In 2022, the total value of green and sustainable debt issued in Hong Kong (including bonds and loans) reached US$80.5 billion, representing a 42% increase. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and commit to developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018, with the HKMA assisting in the implementation of related green bond issuances. To date, the Government has issued green institutional and retail bonds worth nearly US$16 billion, with proceeds allocated to over 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. To enhance transparency and accountability, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report" detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bond issuances and the expected environmental benefits. To enable the public to participate in Hong Kong's sustainable development through investment and share in its benefits, the first tranche of green retail bonds with a total value of HK$20 billion was issued in May, receiving enthusiastic public support and becoming the largest green retail bond issuance globally at the time. This issuance also expanded the range of green and sustainable financial products in Hong Kong, consolidating its status as the premier green finance hub in the region and internationally. The Government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds in the 2022-23 financial year and issued green bonds worth US$5.75 billion in January 2023. This tri-currency issuance covered the US dollar, euro, and renminbi, with maturities ranging from 2 to 30 years, continuing to provide an important benchmark for potential issuers in Hong Kong and the region. The issuance was warmly received by the global investment community and successfully attracted new investors who had not participated in the Government's previous green bond issuances, reflecting investor confidence in Hong Kong's long-term creditworthiness and economic fundamentals. In response to investor demand, the Government doubled the issuance amount of renminbi-denominated bonds to RMB 10 billion. The participation share of international investors and Mainland investors participating via the Bond Connect "Southbound" channel also increased, demonstrating Hong Kong's role as the premier offshore renminbi business hub and further consolidating its leadership as an international financial centre. The HKMA also assisted the Government in issuing tokenised institutional green bonds in February 2023 to test the use of distributed ledger technology for bond issuance and settlement. These are the world's first tokenised green bonds issued by a government. This primary issuance was settled on a T+1 basis on a private blockchain network, and subsequent processes (including coupon payments, secondary market trading and settlement, and redemption at maturity) were also digitalised. The Government's experience in this issuance can serve as a reference for market participants interested in conducting similar bond issuances in the future. To provide the industry with credible and convenient market information, the HKMA continues to collaborate with the Climate Bonds Initiative and the International Capital Market Association to publish annual reports on Hong Kong's and the region's green debt markets. The International Capital Market Association's report indicates that in 2022, Hong Kong became the largest hub in Asia for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances, with a total value of US$27.8 billion, accounting for more than one-third of the regional total. Following the first issuance in 2021, the Shenzhen Municipal Government issued another RMB 5 billion offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in November 2022, including RMB 2.6 billion in green and blue bonds. In the same month, the Hainan Provincial Government also issued its first RMB 5 billion offshore bonds in Hong Kong, including blue and sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable capital between Mainland China and the rest of the world, as well as its enduring status as the region's premier fundraising platform. The HKMA continues to promote and implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in 2021, using it to attract more relevant professional service providers (including financial institutions, green advisory firms, and external review agencies) to establish and expand their businesses in Hong Kong. The scheme has been widely welcomed by the industry. As of the end of 2022, the scheme had covered pre-issuance, post-issuance, or both types of external review service expenditures for over 180 green and sustainable debt instrument issuers, helping issuers ensure and demonstrate strict adherence to market best practices and international standards. Starting from March, the scheme was optimised by lowering the minimum loan amount threshold for applying for external review fee subsidies from HK$200 million to HK$100 million, facilitating access to green financing for smaller enterprises. Following the successful proof-of-concept of tokenised retail green bonds under Project Genesis in 2021, the HKMA and the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub Hong Kong collaborated again under Genesis 2.0 to explore the technical feasibility of digitalised carbon forwards (also known as Mitigation Outcome Interests, or MOIs), thereby enhancing the transparency, objectivity, and environmental integrity of the green bond market. The project was completed in October 2022, successfully developing two prototypes that use blockchain and other related technologies to track, deliver, and transfer digitalised MOIs.

As one of the world's largest asset owners and managers, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plays a pivotal role in promoting green and sustainable finance to support the global climate change agenda. The HKMA is also a pioneer in responsible investment, having led investments in green and sustainable assets as early as 2015. It requires its external investment managers to adopt the Stewardship Code issued by the Securities and Futures Commission and to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Adhering to the principle of "preservation of capital first, long-term appreciation," the HKMA invests prudently and believes that prioritizing ESG factors can unlock long-term sustainable value and mitigate associated risks. In the face of increasingly severe climate change challenges, the HKMA continues to advance its responsible investment journey, including setting a "Net Zero by 2050" target in 2022 and optimizing risk management strategies to enhance the resilience of its asset portfolio, thereby securing more favorable risk-adjusted long-term returns for the Exchange Fund. The HKMA is also actively engaged in building a green and sustainable finance ecosystem, collaborating with like-minded investors and regulators to promote responsible investment, and working with international organizations to develop ESG investment standards. Transparency of climate-related information plays a crucial role in managing climate risks. To fulfill its commitment to support the Glasgow Declaration issued by the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) at the 2021 UN Climate Change Conference and to green the global financial system, the HKMA has made climate-related disclosures for the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) under the Financial Stability Board. a. FCLTGlobal — Focusing Capital on the Long Term b. PRI — Principles for Responsible Investment c. NGFS — Network for Greening the Financial System d. TCFD — Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFI) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle is to prioritize ESG investments that offer risk-adjusted long-term returns comparable to other projects, thereby aligning with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Details of the HKMA's responsible investment framework are available on the HKMA website: The Investment Committee, a sub-committee of the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies, and monitors the progress of integrating ESG factors into investments and the ESG status of the Exchange Fund through regular meeting reports from the Risk Management and Oversight Division of the EFI. As shown in Illustration 1, an ESG Committee established under the EFI, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing all ESG initiatives within the EFI. Proposals discussed and progress updates from each ESG Committee meeting are reported to the Chief Executive of the EFI. Oversight and Governance Structure for Responsible Investment The dedicated task force within the Risk Management and Oversight Division works closely with various investment teams of the EFI to integrate ESG factors and assists the senior management of the EFI in managing ESG and climate-related risks and opportunities across various investment projects: Public Market Investments The Credit, Regulation and Oversight Committee, composed of senior management of the EFI, monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Oversight Division. Furthermore, the Risk Management and Oversight Division participates in the selection, appointment, and oversight processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (see the section "Striving for Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 27). Private Market Investments The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the Risk Management and Oversight Division and the private market investment team for each investment proposal. Concrete evidence continues to demonstrate the significant impact of climate change and associated risks. According to the latest report by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), even assuming full implementation of the "Nationally Determined Contributions" announced by various regions, the estimated global temperature rise by 2100 will still reach 2.1 to 2.4 degrees Celsius, making it difficult to achieve the Paris Agreement target of limiting the global average temperature increase to below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. If regions adopt more proactive policy measures to narrow the temperature gap, the resulting transition risks, coupled with market repricing of assets based on expected future trends and inherent physical risks, will exacerbate pressure on asset valuations. In light of updates to global warming trajectories and model assumptions, the HKMA, leveraging the expertise of external consultants, has further assessed the resilience of the Exchange Fund "portfolio" under a "Rapid Transition" scenario (Illustration 2), building upon the scenarios evaluated in 2021. The "Rapid Transition" scenario incorporates higher transition risk factors in the short, medium, and long terms, assuming that policy changes and technological developments jointly drive a rapid decline in carbon emissions, while multiple asset classes face sudden divestment to maintain the average global temperature increase within 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2100. This scenario broadly aligns with the disorderly scenario recommended by the NGFS for forward-looking climate impact assessments. The "portfolio" can remain resilient in the medium to long term, as a larger proportion of its asset allocation consists of sovereign bonds with lower sensitivity to transition impacts. Sector distribution is key. Low-carbon power and renewable energy assets can benefit from such transitions. Transition risks and asset repricing may impact performance in the short term, particularly for equity assets. Overall, the "portfolio" will face increasingly severe impacts from physical risks that manifest gradually over time. The energy and traditional utilities sectors remain the most vulnerable. Like other modeling approaches, climate scenario analysis has its limitations. The analysis is based on market benchmark sector distributions at the strategic asset allocation level and does not account for the effects of actively selecting specific securities within a sector. Deeper research reveals that investment projects within the "portfolio" are generally more resilient to transition shocks or suffer less severe impacts compared to the market benchmarks of strategic asset allocation. This result reaffirms that the HKMA's responsible investment, focused on combating climate change, can enhance the resilience of the asset portfolio. Climate change trajectories remain uncertain, and scenario analysis methods will continue to evolve with improvements in data quality and policy developments. The HKMA will regularly review relevant scenarios and optimize assessments to more clearly confirm the resilience of the Exchange Fund in the face of climate change. As a long-term investor, the HKMA fully understands the risks and opportunities brought by climate change. The HKMA is committed to further expanding sustainable investments and seizing opportunities related to climate transition, mitigating climate risks, and enhancing long-term portfolio returns. In 2022, the HKMA continued this positive momentum by increasing its holdings of green, social, and sustainable bonds by 50%. In equity investments, the HKMA invested in actively managed equity portfolios with a governance theme and adopted a carbon-reduction strategy favoring low-carbon emission companies for its passive equity portfolios. Additionally, the HKMA is discussing with the dedicated partner of the Exchange Fund's "Long-Term Growth Portfolio" the establishment of a dedicated private equity portfolio to promote green and sustainable development in the Asia region (Illustration 3). Illustration 3: Continued Implementation of Measures to Increase ESG Investments The HKMA has invested in a pan-African wind farm operator. In addition to producing clean energy, this operator places great emphasis on social and natural biodiversity factors. Before the wind farm was established, local villagers used poison bait to prevent predatory animals from killing their livestock, but this inadvertently endangered certain vulture species, which are endangered. Livestock are a vital asset for local villagers. To assist villagers in protecting their livestock, the operator built livestock shelters within the wind farm to protect them from natural predators. Furthermore, the operator employed a bird monitoring team to issue warnings when vultures were attracted by animal carcasses left behind by predators, allowing wind turbines to be shut down to prevent vultures from being struck by the blades. Reducing livestock predation created a win-win situation: on one hand, it safeguarded villagers' livelihoods; on the other, it reduced the number of vultures killed by wind turbines, thereby protecting endangered species. Good ESG practices can bring more business opportunities and open up revenue sources for companies; the following supply chain-related operations serve as an example. The invested company is a comprehensive logistics and warehousing operator in mainland China, specializing in cold-chain pharmaceuticals, chemical products, and high-end consumer goods logistics services. Facing continuously rising ESG operational standards, primarily driven by multinational corporate clients requiring their service providers to meet high carbon-reduction targets consistent with the Paris Agreement, the company hired external consultants to assist in formulating a "Three-Year ESG Plan" to reduce carbon emission density by 50% by or before 2030. This comprehensive carbon-reduction plan yielded significant results even in 2021 alone. The aforementioned ESG measures earned the company the "Low-Carbon Green Management Case" award from the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing. These achievements and accolades enabled the company to secure numerous business opportunities from multinational clients in the consumer and chemical product sectors that particularly value ESG practices. The growth of ESG investment is closely linked to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities. In 2022, the HKMA successfully hosted the 4th Annual ESG Workshop, exchanging best ESG practices with nine participating private market institutions (including general partners, limited partners, and corporations) and promoting sustainable investment opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region and the Greater Bay Area. In the public markets, the HKMA has urged trading partners (primarily investment banks) to expand their ESG personnel and research capabilities, especially in Hong Kong. Mr. David Li, Chief Executive of the EFI, delivered the opening address at the 2022 HKMA ESG Workshop. At the international level, the HKMA actively participates in formulating industry ESG investment standards and practices: As one of the earliest central bank signatories to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA participated in a joint action coordinated by the PRI to develop a unified responsible investment due diligence questionnaire for private equity and venture capital investments, assisting private market investors in conducting ESG assessments of general partners and investment proposals. The HKMA participates in multiple working groups to support FCLTGlobal's research, which aims to explore market best practices for long-term portfolios and decarbonizing private assets, as well as the application of these practices for long-term investors. As a member of the NGFS and a supporter of the TCFD, the HKMA contributed to the NGFS's "Guidance on Climate-related Disclosures for Central Banks" to demonstrate its commitment to adopting good ESG practices. The HKMA also leads a working group under the NGFS's "Central Bank Net Zero" task force to participate in formulating sustainable and responsible investment policies for the central banking sector. The HKMA continues to participate in various industry forums and lectures to share insights on responsible investment and climate change strategies. Ms. Vivian Lau, Chief Risk Officer of the EFI (center), speaks at the ESG Investment Opportunities Sharing Session. Building internal capacity is crucial for continuing the ESG journey. In addition to encouraging employees to pursue relevant sustainability courses and obtain related qualifications, the HKMA has drawn upon relevant knowledge and practical experience from the process where external consultants provided advice on industry best practices for portfolio climate transition in 2021. On the other hand, the HKMA utilizes ESG data compiled by reputable external information providers to supplement its continuous analysis of the asset portfolio, helping to consolidate the ESG resilience of the Exchange Fund.

The HKMA is committed to reducing its own carbon footprint with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, thereby contributing to Hong Kong's overall climate goals. While actively promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfils its commitments to caring for employee well-being, promoting financial inclusion, and upholding social responsibility. The HKMA strives to conduct its daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA implements sustainability principles under three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility (Figure 1). The Institutional Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating and implementing its sustainability strategy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Committee comprises three Deputy Chief Executives and representatives from the Risk Management and Supervision Department and the Institutional Development and Operations Department; it submits regular reports to the Governance Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the leadership of this Committee, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and executing measures within their respective domains. In 2022, the Institutional Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved the HKMA's climate targets for institutional operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review progress on the HKMA's green initiatives, including recommendations to strengthen the HKMA's sustainable procurement policies, procedures, and methodologies. Governance Structure for Sustainability Institutional Sustainability Journey In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to the environment, employees, and society at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service (HKCSS) has, for the 16th consecutive year, awarded the HKMA the "15+ Years of Caring Together" mark. The HKMA places significant emphasis on its own carbon footprint and has developed internal "Green Office Guidelines" to manage the environmental impact of its operational processes. Environmental considerations have been integrated into the interior design, operations, and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded the HKMA Gold certification for certain refurbished office areas. This is the second green building certification obtained by the HKMA, following the LEED Gold certification received in 2021. BEAM Plus Interior Building 1.0 Gold Certification The HKMA implements various energy-saving measures. In 2022, total energy consumption6 was 4,996.4 MWh (2.8 MWh per person7), representing a 24.4% decrease compared to 2015 (Figure 1). Total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions8 in 2022 were 2,996.4 tonnes of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), a 38.2% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse Gas Emission Intensity (Scope 1 and 2) The HKMA encourages paperless operations within the institution. Additionally, the HKMA has implemented a print management system requiring employees to log in to printers to confirm each print request, helping to reduce unnecessary printing and toner usage. Where printing is indeed necessary, double-sided paper use and black-and-white printing are encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic records retention system. In 2022, total paper consumption was 20.5 tonnes (0.0114 tonnes per person), a 65.3% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: Paper Consumption Density The HKMA's waste management continues to adhere to the "4R" principle. In addition to traditional waste, the HKMA reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualization and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company for the first time to conduct a waste audit, analyzing the composition of waste generated in its offices. The audit found that food waste constituted a significant portion of total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see page 41, "Enhanced Waste Management"). Total non-hazardous waste generated in 2022 (including general waste and recyclables) was 242.0 tonnes (0.135 tonnes per person), a 4.8% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 3). The fluctuation in the trend was primarily due to the implementation of work-from-home arrangements during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent resumption of office operations after the fifth wave. Figure 3 Non-Hazardous Waste Density The HKMA prioritizes waste reduction at source and is committed to reducing, reusing, and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to better understand the composition of waste generated in daily operations (plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronics, etc.) and to provide waste reduction recommendations. Based on the audit results, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, installing food waste collection bins in all pantry areas. Daily collected food waste is transported to an organic resource recovery centre in Hong Kong to be converted into renewable energy for power generation. The residue produced during the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscaping and agricultural production. Additionally, recycling bins are located at various points within the offices for convenience. The HKMA shares recycling tips with employees and focuses on further improving source segregation of recyclables, as well as providing guidelines on handling items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. Furthermore, we continue to organize activities to raise employees' environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage the proper use of recycling facilities within the office. Daily collected food waste is transported to an organic resource recycling centre. Recycling of plastic items The HKMA operates two data centres (operational and backup). As these account for a major portion of the institution's total energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green designs and implemented multiple energy-saving measures, including in-row air conditioning systems, LED lighting, and 24-hour monitoring of energy efficiency. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. Preparations have also begun to obtain green data centre certification. Recognizing the importance of building a sustainability culture, the HKMA regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage employees to develop habits conducive to sustainability and to adopt green and digital working methods. The HKMA shares green living tips with employees, along with annual statistics on office-wide energy consumption and paper usage, reminding them to help address environmental issues at an individual level; employees are also encouraged to submit suggestions on sustainability matters. Under the leadership of a Senior Manager in the Administration Group, a task force brings together employees from different departments to brainstorm ideas and specific measures for promoting a green working environment. Task force members also serve as ambassadors when new green initiatives are launched. The HKMA encourages the broader society to adopt more environmentally friendly operational methods and has launched multiple measures to improve operational efficiency for the HKMA, the financial industry, and the economy as a whole, while minimizing resource consumption. The HKMA's "Secure Electronic Transmission of E-Forms" (STET) system is a one-stop platform enabling banks to submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering various periodic returns required weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annually. Another system, "e-Delivery," is a secure electronic communication channel that allows the HKMA to issue notices, guidelines, and other information to banks. Both systems help save a significant amount of paper annually. Regarding the handling of bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless document submission, allowing bank customers to file complaints via electronic channels and online forms. The HKMA is also developing a next-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper-based to digital records. To reduce paper usage, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU)9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including issuing notices, account opening and closure letters, and responding to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, CMU will continue to explore further green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic procedures for internal and external communications. By promoting the use of the Fast and Seamless Payment System "FPS" and stored-value payment instruments, the HKMA encourages the public to adopt electronic payment methods more widely, replacing cash and physical cheques. More information on "FPS" and stored-value payment instruments is available in the chapter "Hong Kong's Status as an International Financial Centre" of the HKMA's 2022 Annual Report. Distributing electronic red packets is simple and convenient, reduces the use of physical red packet envelopes and banknotes, and helps promote sustainability in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA continues to actively promote the use of electronic red packets via various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to use "FPS" or other e-wallet services through online or mobile banking during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organize various activities to attract users to adopt electronic red packets, such as providing festive user interfaces, enhancing functionality for greater convenience, and launching lucky draws or cashback offers. HKMA promotion of electronic red packets on social media For those who choose to give physical red packets during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of "New Year Notes"—banknotes that are old but in crisp condition. Using New Year Notes reduces the need to print new banknotes, thereby minimizing environmental impact. Feedback from note-issuing banks indicates that the public has become increasingly accepting of New Year Notes in recent years. Coin Collection Scheme This scheme reflects the HKMA's efforts in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through the scheme are returned to circulation to meet public demand, improving coin circulation efficiency and reducing the need for minting. The scheme operates two coin collection vans, which have served over one million people to date, collecting more than 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to use part or all of their coin value to top up stored-value payment instrument accounts. The HKMA maintains cooperation with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying coin collection vans on flag-day fundraising events for non-governmental organizations to support social services. Coin counting machine on the coin collection van Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Scheme is the world's first systematic coin collection programme utilizing a mobile van concept. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards, with its innovative and environmentally friendly coin handling methods highly recognized. The scheme operates two coin collection vans, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Citizens can choose to exchange coins for banknotes, use them to top up stored-value payment instrument accounts (such as Octopus cards or e-wallets), or donate them to the Community Chest. In addition to collecting coins, the vans are occasionally deployed for various educational activities (e.g., student visits).

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the climate targets ("Climate Targets") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Climate Targets were developed in reference to the requirements of the Science Based Targets initiative Corporate Handbook ("SBTi Corporate Handbook"). The purpose of this verification engagement is to verify whether the Climate Targets were developed in reference to the SBTi Corporate Handbook. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" standard, ISAE 3000 (Revised), issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Handbook. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes: • The Climate Targets were developed in reference to the SBTi Corporate Handbook. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.  Verification Statement  The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data ("2022 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2022 Data includes total energy consumption for 2022, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensities, paper consumption intensity, and the intensity and recycling rate of non-hazardous waste generated, as well as the changes in these data compared to 2015 levels. The HKMA's GHG emission data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute ("WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development ("WBCSD"). The scope of verification covers relevant data for the period from January 1, 2022, to December 31, 2022, and also includes relevant data for the period from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015, used for comparison of annual performance. The verification scope encompasses a total of six office and warehouse assets: four offices located at 1) International Finance Centre Tower Two, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase One, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre; and two warehouses located at 5) Lo Shing Industrial Centre and 6) Chong Lee Centre, situated in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan, respectively. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the six assets. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" standard, ISAE 3000 (Revised), issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, conducting reliability testing. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and verifying representative data and information. Relevant original data and supporting evidence were also examined in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team did not participate in the preparation process of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2022 Data and concludes: • The 2022 Data are substantially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.

Expanding and accelerating climate action has become the most urgent challenge of our time. We have already passed nearly half of the critical decade for addressing the climate crisis. To have a chance of limiting global warming to within 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, global carbon emissions must be reduced by more than 40% over this decade. Yet, greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window of opportunity to limit global temperature rise to 1.5°C is rapidly closing. The impacts of a 1.1°C temperature increase are already clearly felt: record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding, and storms are occurring with increasing frequency and intensity worldwide. Hong Kong is no exception. Following a fierce super typhoon in September last year, we were immediately hit by a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our robust infrastructure and rapid disaster response capabilities, the impacts were severe—widespread flooding, transportation disruptions, and damage to numerous roads. These events serve as a stark reminder that decisive and proactive climate action is urgently needed. Asia faces particularly significant challenges in its low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We require credible transition strategies that appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Given the region's rapid economic development and fast-growing population, its carbon emissions account for more than half of the global total. Moreover, the Asia-Pacific region's high population density and geographical location make it particularly vulnerable to sea-level rise and extreme weather events. Due to varying stages of economic development within the region, while the low-carbon transition presents new opportunities for some economies, securing the necessary transition financing remains a huge challenge for others. Market estimates suggest that the Asia-Pacific region will require over USD 3 trillion in annual low-carbon transition investments over the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capacity and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia. As the banking regulator, market facilitator, and responsible investor, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has made significant efforts towards the sustainability agenda. This report details the specific measures and initiatives undertaken by the HKMA over the past year. Additionally, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and more effectively coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainable Oversight Committee last year. For detailed information on this committee, please refer to the newly added chapter on "Governance of Sustainability." Hong Kong's banking sector plays a pivotal role in supporting Asia's transition to net-zero emissions. Beyond fulfilling its traditional regulatory functions to ensure banks properly manage climate risks in their daily operations, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, supporting the banking sector in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a Green Classification Framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype of the Green Classification Framework for consultation in May and are currently optimizing the framework based on feedback collected during the consultation period. Furthermore, as the demand for higher-quality and globally comparable sustainable disclosure information grows, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) in June, which constitute a comprehensive global baseline for sustainable reporting. The HKMA's role as a facilitator extends beyond establishing frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing industry pain points. Currently, many banks face data limitations that hinder their ability to conduct physical risk assessments. In response, the HKMA will launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform in the near term. Banks will be able to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios simply by inputting property addresses, thereby assisting them in managing related climate risks. As a major international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has consistently played a bridging role, channeling international investment into sustainable development projects across Asia to support the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total value of international green and sustainable bonds arranged for issuance in Hong Kong has accounted for over one-third of the Asian market, significantly leading other regions. Notably, the governments of Shenzhen and Hainan issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong for the third and second consecutive years respectively in 2023, further affirming Hong Kong's vital role as a green gateway connecting mainland China with the rest of the world. The thriving sustainable bond activity in Hong Kong is partly attributable to the demonstration effect of the "Government Green Bond Programme." Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the government in issuing green bonds worth approximately USD 25 billion to institutional and retail investors. Seizing every issuance opportunity, we have continuously innovated and expanded the features of green bonds, including currency, maturity, and distribution channels, laying a foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bond in 2022, we launched the world's first tokenized government green bonds in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the issuance of the second batch of tokenized green bonds; denominated in four major currencies and issued in a digital-native form, these are the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds. Concurrently, we have proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vitality and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. These efforts span multiple areas, including skills training, data improvement, green fintech, and transition finance. Particularly in talent development, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Banking Professional Qualifications Framework in 2023, providing systematic courses for banking practitioners to enhance their understanding and expertise in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key focus area, providing funding for decarbonization activities in high-carbon and hard-to-abate sectors to prevent these industries from failing to transition due to lack of financial support. To support the robust development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand the scope of Hong Kong's Green Classification Framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the coverage of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme," which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, encouraging enterprises in the region to raise transition financing in Hong Kong. Additionally, we will strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders, leveraging public-private partnerships and blended finance models to attract private sector investment into sustainable development projects that have historically been difficult to finance. Some of the above-mentioned tasks require cross-sectoral collaboration and are primarily coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Committee, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-term collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the "Green Banking Alliance," the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office joined the "Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance" and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" in 2023 as founding members. Furthermore, the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" has announced plans to establish an office in Hong Kong. Through these collaborations, we aim to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channeling of funds to sustainable development projects in the region and globally. To foster new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also assisted in organizing the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 regions, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to discuss ways to expand climate financing in the region and forge new partnerships. Chief Executive Mr. Eddie Yue delivered a speech at the focal event of "Hong Kong Green Week," the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum." As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a significant global asset holder, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been a pioneer in investing in green and sustainable assets, gradually expanding the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolios in both public and private markets. In line with the Exchange Fund's target of achieving net-zero emissions for its "portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA added a new active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition last year, while also expanding the application of a customized low-carbon equity index to another public market asset portfolio. Moreover, the HKMA prioritizes investments in green, socially responsible, and sustainable bonds, which have outperformed their benchmarks, embodying the principle of "doing well by doing good." In the private markets, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. By the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio had decreased by 6% and 46% compared to 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently remained below the overall market level. As a sustainability-focused institution, the HKMA will continue to strive for progress, formulating our sustainability goals and plans based on three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Specifically, in our journey towards low-carbon transition, the HKMA continuously strengthens its capacity to respond to climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emission reduction, energy efficiency improvement, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term and have made good progress towards our interim target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to fulfill the HKMA's various critical functions, in addition to green goals, we are also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our employees. Furthermore, through collaboration with various stakeholders, we promote financial inclusion, enhance citizens' financial literacy, and raise public awareness against financial fraud, contributing to the creation of a caring society. The climate challenge is immense and exceptionally urgent. Economies worldwide are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring significant changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries considerable potential risks but also accompanies unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in action to address these challenges. At the same time, we are well-positioned to seize this momentum. The HKMA will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition; continue to act as a responsible investor and sustainable institution, leading by example, and collaborate with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. Eddie Yue, Chief Executive.

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global concerns. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) aims to demonstrate leadership through its policies and operations in its sustainability work, ensuring that both the Hong Kong financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate-related risks while supporting the transition to a more sustainable economic development path. Through active engagement with international and regional organizations, the HKMA will also contribute to the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector's climate adaptation capabilities and climate risk management. Specifically, key priority tasks include: launching a new thematic review on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting a new round of consultation meetings as part of the assessment of banks' progress in implementing regulatory requirements on climate risk management; continuing work on integrating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review processes; completing the second round of economy-wide climate risk stress tests, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainable disclosure, including collaborating with local relevant authorities to align related regulations with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards as the global benchmark, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Third Pillar 1 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices for transition planning with the industry. To promote the healthy development of banks in offering green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to monitor local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain close contact with the industry to ensure banks adopt appropriate sales procedures. Furthermore, the HKMA will play a facilitator role in promoting the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing economic transitions. We will soon launch a local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to include more activities such as transition activities. Meanwhile, we will continue to explore the application of technology solutions to assist banks in identifying, measuring, and monitoring their climate risk exposures; one example is the upcoming cloud-based platform designed to facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional capabilities of practitioners, we will also develop the professional-level unit on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in 2024. Hong Kong possesses superior conditions to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfill this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing proposals in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope of the "Government Green Bond Programme" to include sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market; simultaneously, through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Fund," we aim to attract more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises to raise green funds via Hong Kong and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in the implementation of the Government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As Co-Chair of the "Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance" (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives to promote the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus on three areas: sustainable disclosure, application of technology, and transition finance. As another key priority, through the "Green Banking Alliance," the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various specialized initiatives in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and delivering practical guidance to assist banks in establishing their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our collaboration with the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero," the "Capacity Building for Sustainable Investment Alliance," and the "Partnership for Green Development Investment and Financing." As a responsible investor, the HKMA commits to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to strengthen the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring the resilience of the asset portfolio in the journey toward net zero. Recognizing that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a comprehensive economic transition, we are optimizing our net-zero strategy to prioritize assets that deliver positive climate benefits to the real economy, while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As an environmentally conscious institution, the HKMA's decarbonization strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest developments in the market, regulation, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further enhance the HKMA's climate adaptation capabilities and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. Additionally, we will continue to actively encourage staff participation in our sustainability initiatives, including launching campaigns to foster sustainable habits and optimizing office processes and practices.
