Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement practices, including evaluating suppliers' ESG practices during contract selection and renewal. Building on the Green Data Centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA commits to adhering to the specified certification standards. Regarding regular updates to data centre facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technological developments, we will also integrate green design and operational practices. Meanwhile, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, while actively modernizing internal systems to improve efficiency and minimize potential risks as much as possible. Finally, regarding social focus areas, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues and collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion, enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness regarding the prevention of financial fraud.

Climate change impacts every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these effects. Through its multiple roles as a central bank, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainability institution, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the wider Asia region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of related measures, and ensures that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and practices. In its commitment to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has put in place a robust sustainability governance framework characterized by clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and establishes effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and provide recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which leads the overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Investment Office; and for other functional areas, relevant task forces and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Cross-Agency Green and Sustainable Finance Steering Group (Steering Group), jointly initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of various financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work in recent years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas. This includes: providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; evaluating the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and supervising external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. Additionally, we invite Executive Directors with primary responsibilities related to green and sustainable development matters to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key achievements and future plans of their respective areas. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups from the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Relations Department, and the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund. In addition to developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the Steering Group, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem."

Climate change represents a significant risk facing the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impacts of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their day-to-day operations. To continue fulfilling their vital role in the financial system and to channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA is dedicated to formulating various policy measures to enhance the banking system's capacity to address climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a Net Zero Transition Planning Notice outlining high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the economy's transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of this Notice, we conducted a questionnaire survey with selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices regarding transition planning with the industry and will organize seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experiences. Regarding disclosure requirements, in response to recent international developments, including the International Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB) published in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's (BCBS) consultation in November on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is strengthening its efforts to improve Hong Kong banks' sustainability-related disclosure framework. Specifically, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the ISSB. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to help banks further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA has made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process. Climate risk management has now been established as a standing agenda item in prudential supervisory meetings with bank management. Banking supervisors have also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system1 that incorporates climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the "Green" Assessment Framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process (SREP) used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risks. Following the completion of the 12-month implementation period for complying with Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, the HKMA launched a thematic review on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. This thematic review covered four key areas: the governance framework for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and organizational culture, awareness, and communication. The HKMA made several improvements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of simultaneous economic and climate change shocks. Following these improvements, and as part of the HKMA's regular regulator-led stress testing program, the second round of climate risk stress testing commenced in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance their climate risk management capabilities. A total of 44 banks participated in this stress test, representing an increase of over 60% compared to the first pilot program in 2021. The HKMA also hosted a Climate Risk Stress Testing Forum in November, attended by up to 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experiences among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other public sources to assess their progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. With growing global attention on climate change and efforts to address it, the HKMA has observed an increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering relevant products to meet customer needs. In light of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review on the sale of green and sustainable investment products by banks and issued a Notice in November outlining the standards the HKMA expects banks to achieve and sharing observed good practices. This Notice covers multiple areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and control, staff training, and record-keeping, aiming to reduce potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, thereby strengthening banks' capacity to manage climate risks. The HKMA is about to launch a beta version of a cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Furthermore, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technology solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to reduce the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby strengthening banks' operational workflows for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organized the "Green Fintech Competition," aiming to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) Net Zero transition or transition planning; (ii) Climate risk management; (iii) Green and sustainable finance; and (iv) Sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submissions from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA held the "Green and Sustainable Banking Seminar," providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and mainland China, and announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition." The event attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators, and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and make green and sustainable financial decision-making more consistent, the HKMA, with the assistance of consulting firms, developed a local green taxonomy framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of the Hong Kong Green Taxonomy Framework" to solicit stakeholder opinions on establishing and implementing a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the framework prototype and identifying other areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF); the FATF has recognized environmental crimes as predicate offenses for money laundering, and given the linkages between AML and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues, this area is receiving increased attention from regulators. Fully aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and the financial sector. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board (FSB), the HKMA participates in analyzing the interplay between transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to adopt a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. In terms of research, the HKMA has conducted multiple applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics include climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG capital flows3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in global supply chains5. These research findings have enhanced the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, aiding in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Internationally, the HKMA also shares research outcomes with a wide range of stakeholders through international activities on climate-related matters and various channels such as the "HKMA Research Memoranda." The HKMA's "Liquidity Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized standby liquidity facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has, in accordance with NGFS recommendations, incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as the mainstream. Through such participation, the HKMA helps facilitate policy dialogue between international and regional bodies on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is committed to enhancing market awareness and engagement, providing necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. Throughout the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a more robust ecosystem and further advance green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Cross-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group), co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the government's climate strategy. Since its establishment, the Steering Group has made significant progress. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to help Hong Kong seize opportunities in sustainable finance, with main areas of work including sustainable disclosure, ecosystem building, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainable Disclosure Working Group has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. This roadmap will cover four key areas: sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Working Group has also been set up to explore methods for supporting financial institutions and enterprises in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group has also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. Particularly in the area of data, we continue to promote the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-Listed Companies, launched in 2022 by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP. The Steering Group will continue to keep pace with the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's status as a regional and global hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to capture investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support industry skills training, the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre under the Steering Group implemented the government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme," providing subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates who undertake relevant training and obtain related qualifications. As of December 2023, 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications were registered as eligible under the scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications were approved. The HKMA also launched the foundational level of a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework." This unit aims to foster talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the banking industry to develop the professional level of this unit to meet the rapidly growing demand for professionals in green and sustainable finance. To help financial institutions and enterprises, especially SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, the HKMA, together with relevant government policy bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), organized a series of seminars and thematic workshops during the year, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. Regarding students, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Programme" in 2022, training sessions were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns' and university bachelor's degree graduates' understanding of sustainable finance. Recognizing the potential of technology in filling climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making such data more accessible and enhancing its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website optimization measures to provide a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, enterprises, and the public. Key enhancements include an electronic platform for sustainable disclosure, tools for calculating and estimating greenhouse gas emissions, and more centralized, user-friendly, and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week," the Steering Group, in collaboration with Cyberport and the Trade Development Council, co-organized the event "Leveraging Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance," showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from February 26 to March 1, 2024, attracting over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, enterprises, central banks, international organizations, government bodies, academia, and consulting firms. The flagship event of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," co-organized by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). The forum brought together over 400 guests, including top decision-makers in global business and finance, to discuss ways to unlock climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. This two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonization of heavy industries, the circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in Asia-Pacific's emerging and developing markets. The event received strong support from both public and private sectors, with over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other exchange activities co-organized. Topics covered included climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomies, and green development financing in the "Belt and Road" region. Additionally, on February 29, 2024, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) co-organized the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" to discuss key measures to scale up climate finance and the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These activities are part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms for participants to drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the IFC and the HKMA launched the "Green Banking Alliance," a collaborative platform bringing together regional financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions, and technology innovators to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 training events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second Frontier Issues Report titled "Developing Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategies: Case Studies." The HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office joined the newly established "Capacity Building for Sustainable Investment Alliance" (CASI) and the "Green Investment and Financing Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the "Belt and Road" International Alliance for Green Development during the year. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more funding towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong office to support net-zero efforts by financial institutions in Hong Kong and mainland China, with the HKMA providing advisory support. To demonstrate the government's commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the "Government Green Bond Programme" was launched in 2018. The HKMA assisted in the issuance of green bonds under the programme. To date, the government has issued approximately USD 25 billion worth of green institutional and retail bonds, with proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. To enhance transparency and accountability, the government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report" detailing the allocation of proceeds and expected environmental benefits. In the 2023/24 financial year, the government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds, issuing approximately USD 6 billion worth of green bonds in June. This tri-currency issuance covered bonds in USD, EUR, and RMB with various tenors, attracting diverse investor categories and generating strong subscription interest, with total subscriptions reaching nearly USD 30 billion. The RMB bond issuance increased from RMB 10 billion in January to RMB 15 billion, and a 10-year RMB bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the government's RMB yield curve and further enrich offshore RMB product offerings. The strong response from global investors to the government's green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the government issued a second tranche of green retail bonds totaling HKD 20 billion, further advancing market development and promoting financial inclusion. This issuance provided citizens with a stable-return investment opportunity, enabling them to both participate in and benefit from Hong Kong's green finance development.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plays a pivotal role in advancing green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, it has led the way in investing in green and sustainable assets, requiring its external investment managers to exercise active ownership and integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Adhering to the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value appreciation," the HKMA invests prudently, believing that due attention to ESG factors helps mitigate related investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a "net-zero by 2050" target for its portfolio, the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment journey. It emphasizes sustainability, particularly the urgent issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and pursue superior risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem. It collaborates with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and among central banks. Through supervision and cooperation, the HKMA is dedicated to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development advance hand in hand.Figure 1: The Exchange Fund's Responsible Investment JourneyComprehensive and reliable ESG information is crucial for integrating sustainability and planning credible climate transitions to achieve net-zero targets. To fulfill its commitments under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) "Glasgow Declaration" and the cross-institutional supervisory task force's strategic plan for green and sustainable finance, the HKMA has taken concrete action. In accordance with recommendations from the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), this chapter outlines the responsible investment practices of the Exchange Fund. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the management of the Exchange Fund's investments. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while maintaining the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee, a sub-committee of the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund's investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team within the EFIO. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring all ESG-related work within the EFIO. Motions and progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the EFIO. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive of the EFIO and the Chief Strategy Officer, meets biannually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG goals.Figure 2: Governance Structure for Responsible Investment at the Exchange Fund Investment OfficeAs illustrated in Figure 1, the EFIO embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could impact the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainability has rapidly evolved, transcending risk considerations to become a key strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the EFIO re-evaluated its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone: the EFIO established a new Business Strategy Department led by the Chief Strategy Officer, responsible for coordinating and leading the EFIO's strategic development. This department incorporated the dedicated responsible investment team previously under the Risk Management and Supervision Department, now renamed the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA's shift in focus for responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related investment matters. The Sustainable Investment Team collaborates closely with various teams within the EFIO on integrating ESG factors and assists senior management in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across different investment projects:Public Market Investments – The Credit, Regulation, and Supervision Committee, composed of senior personnel from the EFIO, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the Sustainable Investment Team's input. It monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Supervision Department. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment, and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 40).Private Market Investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal.The HKMA recognizes that the physical and transition risks, as well as related opportunities, arising from climate change will affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2023 Emissions Gap Report" projects that unless greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced globally, the average global temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more ambitious policies, technological development, or behavioral changes to control temperature rise may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranding. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional physical risks to investment projects. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund; therefore, it places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG considerations. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund's portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonization and transition. The following sections will detail these approaches.Figure 3: The HKMA's Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible InvestmentIn the journey toward net-zero, the HKMA prefers proactive engagement over divestment or exclusion from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition that possess superior technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding related investments or divesting does not help solve the carbon emission problem. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership, driving them to implement transitions to sustainable and low-carbon operational methods, thereby creating beneficial changes for themselves and the globe. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy to pursue transition outcomes that align with the Exchange Fund's and global net-zero targets through a comprehensive approach, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Figure 4).The HKMA's responsible investment maintained strong momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, managed by an external investment manager, and expanded the application of customized low-carbon equity indices to another asset portfolio managed by an external investment manager. Furthermore, the performance of green, social, and sustainable bonds prioritized by the HKMA outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the concept of "doing well by doing good." In private markets, the HKMA actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as climate and energy transitions. For instance, during the year, the HKMA invested in two transition-focused funds primarily targeting Asia, reflecting its commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs.Figure 4: Continuous Implementation of Measures to Promote ESG InvestmentThe HKMA has invested in a company specializing in producing eco-friendly thermoplastic materials from unclassified household waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on high-energy, high-temperature environments to produce plastics, this company pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This 100% waste-derived plastic material can serve as a substitute for oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and durable consumer goods, offering a sustainable and versatile option. Moreover, this plastic material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company firmly supports the circular economy. The diagram below illustrates the positive environmental outcomes resulting from its advanced plastic production process:Managed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the Multi-Client Private Placement (MCPP) is an innovative initiative that combines capital from institutional investors with the IFC's own funds to expand sustainable financing for private companies in emerging markets. The HKMA committed two tranches of USD 1 billion each to the MCPP in 2017 and 2019. It further collaborated with the IFC to create a new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet," in 2021. This is the world's first cross-sector emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP program, the HKMA has committed to providing loans for 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate, and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The IFC has collected data on MCPP loans. According to the IFC's report, the HKMA's loan commitments support emerging markets and developing countries in various areas such as economic transformation and human resource development. Specifically, projects financed by the HKMA are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent annually, equivalent to the emissions from a typical gasoline car driving 14 billion miles.Figure 5: Projected Average Annual Benefits of the HKMA's Loan Commitments to MCPP Since 2020The green and sustainable finance ecosystem is the cornerstone of future global sustainable development. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organization, adopting a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA places emphasis on employee well-being and corporate social responsibility, while striving to advance financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible institution, the HKMA has set sustainability objectives under three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Established in October, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (the Steering Committee)1, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the primary decision-making body for all organizational sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee succeeded the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategies, and policies for organizational sustainability and social responsibility. At the departmental level, the Deputy Chief Executive (Institutional Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Services Task Force provide support for coordinating organizational sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for discussing how to create a green working environment and foster collective ideas, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transformation journey. Key priorities include implementing carbon reduction strategies in its daily operations, such as operating green buildings and data centers, practicing green mobility, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools, and more environmentally friendly operational models, reducing waste, and fostering a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to utilize carbon footprint tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, while adopting carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the above environmental commitments related to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce greener operational solutions for the broader society, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and make contact, as well as electronic payment and coin collection schemes available to the general public. To strengthen and maintain its operational capacity, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and emphasizes employee well-being. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers social enterprises in its procurement processes; promotes consumer education in financial services; and collaborates with the banking sector to ensure equitable access to basic banking services for all sectors of society. The remainder of this chapter details the aforementioned strategies. Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee2, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats the HKMA faces in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. Physical impacts of climate change, such as increased extreme weather events causing flooding or other damage, may affect the HKMA's offices and impede employee travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plan to address extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation exercises to ensure employees are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. The design of its offices also incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy consumption, air travel, and waste management. The HKMA has been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking its greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across all scopes of its organizational operations (Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3, including air travel) by 2050 or earlier. As an interim emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the baseline year, reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various carbon reduction and offset strategies. Although there are challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multi-pronged approach within practical limits to minimize greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 3 (e.g., paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and interim emission reduction targets were developed with reference to the methodology of the "Science Based Targets initiative," which has also been validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has appointed the HKQAA to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper usage, and waste data disclosed in this report6. The scope and criteria for verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the "2022 Annual Report," the HKMA issued its "2022 Sustainability Report" independently for the first time. The HKMA's enhanced ESG reporting efforts have been recognized, receiving the ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023." The HKMA is the first financial regulatory authority to receive an award in this category. The adjudication panel commended the HKMA for achieving high ESG standards, noting that the "Sustainability Report" is clear and easy to read, and that appointing an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to high transparency and accountable reporting. Furthermore, the HKMA received the highest rating, the Gold Award, in the "Non-profit and Charitable Organizations" category at the Hong Kong Management Association's "2023 Best Annual Report Awards." The adjudication panel praised the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and effectively utilizing infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's determination to enhance financial literacy and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years+ Caring Together" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts of its operations, and its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide employees with guidance on resource utilization and office waste generation. The HKMA has integrated environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. During office renovations, existing furniture and decoration materials are reused as much as possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly construction and decoration materials are prioritized. The HKMA has consistently followed this practice, and as a result, received Gold certification under LEED7 and the "BEAM Plus Interior Assessment"8 in 2021 and 2022 respectively for the renovated parts of its offices at Two International Finance Centre. Adopting new technologies and making optimal use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remains one of the HKMA's key focus areas. In addition to promoting good habits, such as turning off unnecessary lighting within work areas outside of office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using LED lighting equipment, motion sensors, setting air conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimizing energy use in IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decrease, reaching 2.59 MWh per person in 2023, a 29.7% reduction from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions primarily stem from electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuels and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e per person, a 45.2% reduction from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardizing equipment, office software, and conference facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, and built a digital working environment to enhance online collaboration within the organization.11 Paperless meetings have become the HKMA's primary mode of conducting meetings. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, most internal administrative matters are primarily handled through electronic processes. Furthermore, the HKMA encourages employees to integrate green and digital working modes, replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, work is underway to implement an electronic records management system. The aforementioned green and digital measures have yielded positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per person, a significant 64.8% reduction from 2015 (Figure 3). Following the post-pandemic recovery, most international activities have returned to physical formats, and to promote the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial center, it is inevitable that relevant HKMA employees need to travel overseas for official business. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages employees to take direct flights or combine different official trips whenever feasible when participating in overseas activities. At the organizational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. Additionally, the HKMA participates in the "Gold Standard"12 certified carbon offset program to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this program implements waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and provides efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process considers sustainability and environmental factors. As part of a comprehensive review of the organization's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalized and adheres to the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List," particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into the tender evaluation criteria. At the same time, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. Following the "4R" principle, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimize waste generation and manage waste disposal. Additionally, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in developing targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are included in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated in the red envelope recycling program organized by the building management company of the International Finance Centre office building for the first time. Employees handed over approximately 3,000 used but still pristine red envelopes. These red envelopes were subsequently given to an environmental organization for distribution to the public for use during the following Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operations and backup data centers constitute the major portion of the organization's total energy consumption, both data centers have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centers, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)13. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centers received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the 2021 assessment guidelines "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centers"; the HKMA is the first and only organization in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centers has always been a key focus of the Technical Team. To this end, the team adopted green design principles in renovation works and implemented good practices compliant with energy efficiency to lower PUE and achieve relevant targets, including 24-hour monitoring of environmental facilities in the data centers and continuously improving environmental factors such as air flow and temperature settings. As the Technical Team continuously improved energy utilization in the data centers, the HKMA commissioned an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green level of the data centers and formulate recommendations for further enhancing performance in various aspects. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the study, the HKMA began preparing to obtain "Green Data Center" certification under the "BEAM Plus" certification scheme. The certification process is extremely comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the Technical Team implemented optimization measures based on the consultant's recommendations to enhance energy performance as well as the health elements of the working environment within the data centers.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2023 Data comprises total energy consumption for 2023, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, business aviation travel GHG emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), their respective intensities, and the changes in these figures compared to 2015 levels. Additionally, the 2023 Data includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the baseline level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's GHG emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste quantities). The verification scope collectively covers five office and warehouse assets: four offices located at 1) International Finance Centre Phase Two, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Swire Plaza Phase One, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and one warehouse at 5) Lothian Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, HKQAA reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the five assets. This verification was performed in accordance with the "International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. Verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion to achieve a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. It tested the completeness and accuracy of data by tracing selected sample data to their sources, and reviewed and tested the reliability of fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and checking selected representative data and information. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work was conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: the 2023 Data is substantially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate.  Shen Siu-yen, Audit Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024.

The threats posed by climate change are imminent, making accelerated global climate action imperative. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed 2024 as the warmest year on record, marking the first time global temperatures have exceeded the critical 1.5°C threshold above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions saw a slight moderation during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. In the process of addressing global warming, climate-related risks are poised to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Furthermore, the current tense geopolitical landscape, an increasingly fragmented global economic structure, escalating energy security concerns, and an uncertain economic outlook all present greater challenges for nations in their efforts to combat climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Globally, Asia faces the most severe transition challenges. As noted by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to climate change impacts. Consequently, Asia plays a pivotal role in determining whether the global community can successfully achieve net-zero emission targets. As Asia's leading international financial centre, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role, fully leveraging financial power to support and drive regional transformation. To this end, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainability principles into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on two fronts: enhancing the financial sector's capacity to manage climate-related risks, and assisting the industry in seizing related new opportunities. Simultaneously, we lead by example. The HKMA's sustainability efforts encompass four key areas: supporting the banking sector's journey towards net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, facilitating net-zero financing, and promoting more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a critical role in Hong Kong and Asia's net-zero transition, yet it faces significant risks in the process itself. In the "Action Plan," we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive for net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions from their financing portfolios by 2050 or earlier. We also require all banks to enhance disclosures regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening banks' climate risk management, we provide guidance for their transition planning, assisting them in enhancing their transition capabilities and better managing associated risks. We are also collaborating with relevant stakeholders to prepare for aligning Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further improve industry transparency in related activities. Additionally, we are optimizing the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy launched last May by incorporating more sustainable activities, including transition activities. We expect that by providing clear criteria, we can guide more capital towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of Exchange Fund investment portfolios. However, it also presents opportunities for growth and driving positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainable impacts can be aligned without conflict. Recognizing this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "investment portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and have committed in the "Action Plan" to supporting Asia's climate transition through Exchange Fund investments. Currently, sustainable investments account for over 10% of the "investment portfolio." To further promote regional sustainable investment, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation last November, accelerating low-carbon economic transformation in Asia through co-investment. Additionally, we released our first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document last September to further encourage fund managers to proactively exercise ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Capital mobilization is particularly crucial for accelerating regional transformation. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including mainland Chinese provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays a vital role in guiding capital to accelerate regional transformation. The "Action Plan" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's premier sustainable finance platform and sets goals to promote sustainable financial innovation. From leveraging the demonstrative effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme" to include transition financing tools last May, and launching the "Digital Bond Funding Scheme" last November, we have consistently encouraged regional issuers to utilize Hong Kong's financial platform to raise funds for decarbonization and transformation. Achieving a robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also an inclusive and accessible sustainable development ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainable development data, high-transparency information disclosure, and industry professionals with relevant knowledge and skills. Accordingly, in the "Action Plan," we committed to supporting the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and to bridging the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainable disclosure among small and medium-sized enterprises. We also launched a professional-level unit on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework last November to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Furthermore, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held last February and other events, we have engaged the public in discussions on sustainable development, fostering collaboration and innovation. Internally at the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring our operations align with our sustainability vision. In the "Action Plan," we committed to achieving net-zero emissions from our own operations by 2030 or earlier, twenty years ahead of our original commitment. Additionally, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the government's roadmap. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening factor in our procurement processes. Simultaneously, we continue to improve efficiency through digitalization, fostering a sustainability culture within the organization and motivating employees to actively participate in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of global climate action, but the reshaping of the international landscape and drastic geopolitical shifts have added variables to global climate efforts. However, climate change is an undeniable fact and is gradually intensifying. In addressing climate change, the current situation allows for no slackening of efforts. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system while creating opportunities for us in the process. Entering 2025, we will continue to forge ahead with determination, striving to advance our sustainability work and deepen relationships with like-minded partners. Despite facing severe challenges, we will, as always, remain committed to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the current generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in the Asia region, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and globally. In October 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), which outlines the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving various objectives, and how we expect the industry to collaborate in advancing these efforts. The HKMA plans to consolidate the resilience of Hong Kong's financial sector and its own capacity to address climate-related risks, while promoting the transition of the Asia region towards a more sustainable economy, by formulating strategic policies, strengthening regulatory engagement, and enhancing internal operations. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA is also committed to exerting influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the banking sector's climate resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during their transition to net-zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting the third round of consultation meetings to examine banks' implementation of relevant HKMA regulatory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - refining the integration of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's supervisory-led stress testing framework; - continuing to advance the incorporation of climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review processes; - commencing preparatory work to formulate relevant regulatory provisions for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming third pillar disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards by the local banking sector; - completing the drafting of a new section, GS-2, in the "Supervisory Policy Manual" to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. Beyond its role as the banking sector regulator, the HKMA also acts as a catalyst, striving to promote the development of a green and sustainable finance ecosystem and support banks in providing financing for the transition. We have released the first phase of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy," providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating related capital flows. The HKMA has commenced work on the second phase of the Taxonomy to expand its coverage, including the incorporation of transition elements, the addition of green economic activities, and the inclusion of climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green FinTech Competition in 2023, we will organize another green fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks to adopt green fintech solutions. Hong Kong possesses superior conditions to support regional sustainable financing needs. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme," whose expanded scope will now include sustainable projects, such as social responsibility initiatives. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a model for other potential issuers in the region. Additionally, we will continue to provide funding through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Financing Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to utilize Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable capital. We will also strengthen our promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from mainland China and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing funding through the "Digital Bond Financing Scheme" to prospective issuers of digital green bonds. Although market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures from institutions and enterprises is increasing, different entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make such disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In response, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Inter-agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance to make sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a richer set of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainable disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can be leveraged to make existing resources more convenient and accessible; and partner with major local industry organizations to deliver industry-specific training. The sustainable finance market is rapidly evolving, necessitating the expansion of the local talent pool and the bridging of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key priorities for 2025 include collaborating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, and identifying areas where further industry training is needed through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study. Additionally, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" and review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Green Banking Alliance" to launch targeted initiatives in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, fostering community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps to integrate green finance into their core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "portfolio" by 2050 or earlier to support the broader economic transition. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approaches, primarily focusing on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can deliver positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in organizational sustainability. In response to the accelerated timeline for achieving net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan," the HKMA will progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting through pragmatic steps, continuing to drive organizational sustainability. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring our focus remains on material matters. Additionally, we will conduct an energy audit and utilize technology solutions to assess the significant impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the government's "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap" and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects based on energy efficiency and energy conservation principles. We will also expand digital measures to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the public.

Climate change impacts every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these effects. Through its multiple roles as the central bank, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainability institution, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of related measures, and ensures that sustainability factors are integrated into the Authority's own operations and methodologies. In its commitment to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has built a comprehensive sustainability governance framework featuring clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively embedded in the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and it establishes effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and provide recommendations; - The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which provides leadership at the management level on the Authority's overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies and policies; - In the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees ESG-related activities within the Office; and - For other functional areas, relevant task forces and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Cross-Agency Steering Group), jointly established by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work over recent years, the Steering Committee was established in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability activities across the Authority's different functional areas. Its responsibilities include: - Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters in four functional areas: banking, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; - Evaluating the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG goals; and - Overseeing external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. Additionally, Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC jointly established the Cross-Agency Steering Group in May 2020. Serving as a cross-agency platform, the Cross-Agency Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts within the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the Cross-Agency Steering Group, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem."

Climate change poses risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to enhancing the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system against climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impacts of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a pivotal role in the financial system by directing capital towards green and sustainable projects.
