As the banking regulator, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), which outlines the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and to support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Plan comprises eight objectives across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the relevant banking policy objectives, we have undertaken the following initiatives. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions from their financed portfolios by 2050 or earlier. All banks are increasing transparency regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched industry consultation on the draft of Unit GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new Unit aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to manage the net-zero transition and associated risk management. Furthermore, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements. The objective is to incorporate factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks, including transition planning, to address climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Standards and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analyzing the latest developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy (the "Taxonomy") to address industry concerns regarding greenwashing and to assist in directing capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, aiming to align with the Common Green Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating relevant elements tailored to local circumstances. We have initiated the second phase of work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting widely with stakeholders to further facilitate the mobilization of green and sustainable capital. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and remained committed to supporting banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all tasks related to integrating climate risks into the banking supervisory process, as set out in the two-year plan formulated in 2022. To facilitate banks in strengthening their climate risk management capabilities, the HKMA shared good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings with the banking industry. These primarily include: - Establishing a robust governance structure that clearly defines the responsibilities of the board of directors and senior management; - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters: (1) Promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) Exercising appropriate oversight over climate-related risk management; and (3) Fostering a strong climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a Balanced Supervision Roundtable on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including challenges banks face in managing climate risks, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and assisted the HKMA in its work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a thematic review of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations outlined in Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic review covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to the specific circumstances of individual banks to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the Banking Sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with participation from 21 retail banks and 25 Hong Kong branches of international banking groups. The results indicate that under various scenarios, including those assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and macroeconomic downturns, the Hong Kong banking sector continues to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot programme, participating banks have significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report detailing the CRST results and good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. Recognizing the numerous challenges banks face regarding data and methodologies in climate risk management, the HKMA has been committed to various initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to evaluate the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform based on user feedback and by incorporating more local data. Additionally, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we released an application practice guide and two RegTech Use Case Briefs (in English) outlining technological solutions for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third "FiNETech" event, bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. The HKMA fully understands that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; therefore, it has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various Financial Stability Reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and the financial sector. In November, the NGFS published the fifth version of its Long-Term Climate Macro-Financial Scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessment. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analyzing the interplay between transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to view climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practice Guide on Banks' Application of Green Technology" (in English) to provide financial institutions with best practices on leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. In terms of research, the HKMA has conducted multiple applied research projects exploring the impacts of climate change on the financial sector and the overall economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in resisting monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition to a low-carbon economy. These research findings not only deepen our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies assist the HKMA in strengthening its ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings are also shared with a wide range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, such as the "HKMA Research Memorandum." The Hong Kong Centre for Monetary Research (the Centre), which is responsible for research under the HKMA's Financial College, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission enterprises can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing and highlights its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission enterprises. The study was published in the Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized standby liquidity facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has already incorporated sustainable considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on responding to climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as mainstream. Through this participation, we help facilitate policy dialogue between international and regional entities on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw upon these insights to enhance the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is committed to enhancing market awareness and engagement, providing necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the HKMA's "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), the Authority is dedicated to elevating the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to establishing Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green sector of financial markets, enhancing industry sustainable disclosure, and expanding the local pool of green talent while addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Transforming Hong Kong into the region's and global preferred sustainable financing platform catalyzes sustainable finance innovation, supports high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and fills the regional talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the "Government Green Bond Programme" was launched in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds equivalent to approximately USD 28 billion to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, including green buildings, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currency, tenor, and distribution channels, laying a foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the programme's impact and further consolidate Hong Kong's status as a green and sustainable finance hub, the programme's scope was expanded to include sustainable projects, and it was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (the "Sustainable Bond Programme"). To improve transparency and accountability, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report," detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bond issuances and their expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing institutional green bonds equivalent to approximately USD 3 billion under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This three-currency issuance included bonds in Renminbi, US dollars, and Euros with varying tenors. These bonds attracted participation from diverse investor categories, receiving an oversubscription of over USD 15 billion. Notably, the 20-year and 30-year Renminbi green bonds marked the Government's first issuance of such tenors, representing the longest-dated Renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date. They provide new benchmarks for the market and further demonstrate the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enrich the selection of offshore Renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the strong response from global investors to the Government's green bonds reflects investor confidence in Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more regional borrowers to utilize Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable development funds, the HKMA continues to implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in May 2021, providing grants for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. Widely welcomed by the industry, as of the end of 2024, the scheme has granted funding for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value exceeding USD 140 billion. The scheme was extended by three years to 2027 in May 2024, with its scope expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of this extension and expansion is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to utilize Hong Kong's transition financing platform to gradually reduce carbon emissions. - Grants awarded for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value exceeding USD 140 billion (as of end-2024). - Extended by three years to 2027, with scope expanded to include transition financing instruments. Meanwhile, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, achieving desirable results. For instance, in August, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued its fourth offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 7 billion, comprising RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 900 million in social responsibility bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People's Government made its first offshore bond issuance in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued its third offshore bonds in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable capital between Mainland China and the rest of the world. Through these measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, in 2024 Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances, with a total value of USD 43.1 billion arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyze sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two batches of landmark tokenized green bonds in 2023 and 2024: the world's first tokenized government green bonds and the world's first multi-currency digital bonds. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for market participants in the region in applying asset digitization and innovative technologies in the fields of green and sustainable finance. In November, the HKMA also launched the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovation and development in the local green and sustainable finance market. The Working Group on Sustainable Disclosure under the Cross-Agency Steering Committee on Green and Sustainable Finance (the "Steering Committee") has been working on the adoption of the "International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Standards" in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government released the "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap," providing a clear path for large public interest entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at various stages of preparation in achieving high-quality sustainable disclosure, making it more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the application of the "Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Unlisted Companies" (the "Questionnaire"), launched in 2022 by the Steering Committee in collaboration with CDP. This questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template, facilitating sustainable disclosure for enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to facilitate online completion by enterprises (see the QR code below). The HKMA is optimizing the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, with specific measures including identifying core questions within the Questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios. Additionally, we are striving to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Committee's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example, making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its "Sustainability Report" in accordance with the latest global standards to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content regarding the HKMA's climate-related operational risks, as well as plans and implementation progress towards achieving climate goals. For details on our own operational sustainable disclosures, please refer to the chapter "A Sustainable HKMA." Given the rapidly evolving nature of the sustainable finance market, to address knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening skills training in the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking professionals in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the foundational level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in July 2023. This unit aims to assist banking professionals in acquiring knowledge and developing relevant professional competencies in green and sustainable finance more effectively, covering four main areas of work: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance Products and Services; (2) Sustainable/Climate Risk Management; (3) Sustainable Disclosure and Reporting; and (4) Sustainable Strategy, Compliance, and Control. Furthermore, the professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit, targeted at mid-to-senior level banking professionals responsible for relevant work, was launched in November. To provide necessary training to banking professionals, the HKIB, as the administering body for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit, launched the foundational level training course in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking industry in 2025 to develop training courses for the professional level. To understand the banking industry's further skills and training needs, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking industry on the research project "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030," with the aim of publishing the results in 2025. This joint research follows up on the document "Future Banking Talent 2021-2025" published in June 2020. The results of the follow-up study will provide important references for the industry to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures, supporting the sustainable development of the banking sector. The HKMA also continues to assist in the implementation of the Government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" through collaboration with the Steering Committee, providing funding for practitioners, graduates, and students to receive sustainable finance-related training. As of December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses were registered as eligible training courses under the scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications have been approved. The Government announced in the "2025-26 Budget" that the scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the "Coalition of Action for Sustainable Investment" (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Finance Promotion Office co-organized a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. Additionally, the HKMA supports the establishment of a branch of the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Leveraging its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to the principles of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritizes sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights. Guided by the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value appreciation," the HKMA invests prudently, believing that a comprehensive focus on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As a steadfast signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the urgent issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and pursue superior risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to investment partners through an annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and among central banks. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, mobilizing partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, and further consolidating its pledge to invest in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the EFIO. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring various ESG initiatives within the EFIO. Motions and progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the EFIO. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive of the EFIO and the Chief Strategy Officer, holds regular meetings to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different HKMA functions, including the EFIO, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the EFIO on integrating ESG factors and assists senior EFIO personnel in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment projects: - Public Market Investments: The Credit, Regulation, and Monitoring Committee, composed of senior EFIO personnel, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the Sustainable Investment Team's opinions and monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring Department. Furthermore, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment, and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 39 for details). - Private Market Investments: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA recognizes that the physical and transition risks, as well as associated opportunities, posed by climate change will affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2024 Emissions Gap Report" projects that unless there is a rapid, large-scale global mobilization to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties regarding policy changes, technological developments, and behavioral shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also bring additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investment projects. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries toward sustainable solutions creates potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG considerations. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund "portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier and is continuously advancing this goal through an orderly three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA published the "Action Plan," which consolidated the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA tends to engage proactively rather than exclude or divest from investable projects. Investing in a Sustainable Future: Achieving Net-Zero Emissions for the Exchange Fund "Portfolio" by 2050 or Earlier - Actively expanding the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly those themed around climate transition in public and private markets. - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with special attention to climate change and transition prospects. - Establishing clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, requiring all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties to comply. - Committing to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030 or earlier. Supporting Regional Transition through Investment - Continuing to communicate with external investment managers to optimize investment opportunities that drive transition. - Continuing to identify and prioritize high-quality investment opportunities that facilitate the Asian transition and generate positive global impact. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial for achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition that possess excellent technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding related investment projects or divesting does not help solve carbon emission issues. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising ownership rights, driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon operational methods, thereby bringing beneficial changes for themselves and the global community. The net-zero investment strategy has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects to drive comprehensive carbon reduction across the entire economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of an asset portfolio depends not only on the portfolio's own adjustments but also on broad economic transformation. Although there is no perfect single solution, the HKMA improved its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting both the Exchange Fund's and the global net-zero goals. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors into fundamental analysis and stewardship, tilting the portfolio toward decarbonization, and making thematic investments in various assets aligned with the path to net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio toward ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, the focus may be more on investment projects that facilitate transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund asset portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund "portfolio," with financial performance comparable to the respective asset class benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public Market Investments: The HKMA has launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition and has extended the application of customized low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social, and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while funding sustainable projects (see the case study section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds"). - Private Market Investments: The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA actively identifies and reviews investment opportunities that can accelerate energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with cross-border organizations (see examples in the section "Jointly Addressing Climate Challenges from Asia to the Globe"). - Passive portfolios using ESG indices as benchmarks. - Customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios whose benchmarks are not ESG indices. - Active portfolios themed on governance. - Active ESG portfolios themed on sustainability and climate transition. - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and buildings and warehouses with green certification. - Funds themed on energy transition and carbon reduction globally, in Asia, and in the Global South. - Green, social, and sustainability bonds. - A green bond fund managed by an international organization. - The "Multi-Currency Portfolio Management Program" (MCPP) managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets. - The "MCPP One Planet" project, providing emerging market climate-related investments compliant with the Paris Agreement. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a semi-official institution. The funds raised from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading aging equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects cover optimizing monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuously treating wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or reuse dehydrated sludge to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize gases generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond funds multiple projects, including the restoration of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess water from rivers to arid regions. The primary objective of the project is to restore the deteriorating canal lining to prevent leakage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. Additionally, the project provides skills training for local stakeholders and promotes the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming methods.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is committed to becoming a responsible and sustainable institution. One of the HKMA's key priorities in 2024 to fulfill this commitment is to advance its target date for achieving net-zero emissions from institutional operations to 2030, which is 20 years earlier than the original target, aligning with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan." In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is committed to fostering staff training and well-being, advancing financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the primary decision-making body for all institutional sustainability measures. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 the new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions from its institutional operations by 2030 or earlier as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Executive Director (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures related to institutional operations, staff well-being, and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Group acts as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on institutional sustainability measures. Green Office Working Groups and Volunteer Service Groups, composed of staff from various operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former serves as a platform to brainstorm and propose suggestions on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, staff, and society at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years+ Care Together" mark for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: environment, staff, and social responsibility. Key initiatives include: focusing on decarbonization and digitalization in the HKMA's daily operations with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier; adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines; promoting more environmentally friendly operational practices to the financial sector and the broader society; building a positive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives; fostering a collaborative and caring working environment that values diversity and strengthens staff sense of belonging; providing a quality working environment to promote healthy lifestyles; cultivating a culture of social care; incorporating social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management; and promoting financial inclusion while enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education activities. The HKMA is concerned about climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to advance its target date for achieving net-zero emissions from its institutional operations to 2030, which is 20 years earlier than its original commitment, as part of the "Action Plan." The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards a net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, conserving energy, reducing paper usage, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix of local power generators. Furthermore, the HKMA has established a digital working environment to improve efficiency and simultaneously reduce its carbon footprint. Additionally, recognizing the importance of cultivating a sustainability culture, the HKMA encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programs and activities. Under the primary 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the adoption of carbon embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and pursue low-carbon procurement wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset schemes. The HKMA will expand its carbon embedded and carbon offset programs to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the aforementioned environmental commitments regarding actual operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, ranging from launching electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for return to circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting staff well-being and social care. Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and examined their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, HKMA offices are designed with multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. Furthermore, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only office premises but also communication and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation exercises to ensure staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also continuously monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions generated by its operations, waste generation, as well as energy consumption and paper usage. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from institutional operations across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 by 2030 or earlier. These targets were developed with reference to the methodology of the "Science Based Targets initiative." The HKMA adopts the "Greenhouse Gas Protocol" to measure and report institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions originate from direct emissions from gasoline vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's primary greenhouse gas emissions are indirect Scope 2 emissions resulting from the consumption of fossil fuels to generate electricity. Due to the lack of data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital products) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are included in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" attached at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards expected of the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its gasoline vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and decoration materials or traded in old items for new ones at a discount, thereby reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in offices and data centers, and adopted an uninterruptible power supply system with modular design in the 2024 data center facility upgrade project, further optimizing the energy usage efficiency (Power Usage Effectiveness, or PUE) of its data centers certified under the "BEAM Plus" scheme. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency under partial load conditions, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA strengthens internal virtual collaboration through digital workspaces, coupled with streamlined workflows, effectively reducing paper usage. Additionally, by extending the usage period of mobile and desktop devices in accordance with manufacturers' software update cycles, the HKMA can extend the safe usage period of these devices. To reduce waste generated in offices, the HKMA adheres to the "4R" principles: Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has installed recycling bins for different materials at multiple convenient locations within its offices. To improve recycling rates, the HKMA added recycling bins for drink cartons and plastic fruit mesh bags in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy center in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Commitment," pledging to take measures to reduce waste generated from various events. The HKMA continues to prioritize the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List," particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to carefully plan their trips, such as combining multiple journeys when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, since 2023, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel, reducing annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. Additionally, the HKMA participates in the "Gold Standard" certified carbon offset scheme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this scheme focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA organized various learning activities for staff, such as lectures and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on April 22, 2024, through the entire month of May, the HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month" with the theme "Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Working." This served as an excellent opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA's commitment and drive to practice environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The event included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to practice green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and an indoor plant care workshop on "Kokedama" originating from Japan; it also featured the sharing of waste audit results and an introduction to best practices in recycling by community recycling center operators. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," the HKMA launched a recycling campaign in October lasting approximately six months, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that aggregating small changes in individual habits can significantly improve the overall recycling performance of the institution. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of the "Green 'Fit' Action" short video, in which several senior staff members shared recycling tips. The campaign also introduced a series of screensavers, distinctive posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to encourage staff to take personal action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to understand their awareness of sustainability and gather their opinions on proposed green office measures. The survey results will assist in formulating future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking authority, the HKMA views itself as a key player in driving change and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of low-carbon transitions, promoting sustainable operational practices across the financial sector and society at large. The HKMA has launched multiple measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the "Shared Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored-value payment facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The purpose of expanding the platform's service scope is to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures launched in 2024 include SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys via a simplified submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system, providing a central platform for users with advanced search functions for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has conducted an independent verification of the environmental data ("Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Data includes total energy consumption for 2024, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and GHG emissions from air travel, along with their respective intensities. Additionally, the Data includes Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's GHG emissions Data has been prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol), jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covers a total of six office and warehouse assets: five offices located at 1) International Finance Centre Phase 2, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase 1, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre; and one warehouse at 6) Lo Shing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative Data and supporting evidence selected from the six assets. This verification was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion to achieve a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. It tested the completeness and accuracy of the Data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed and tested the reliability of fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and verifying representative data and information. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the Data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - The Data is substantially accurate and reliable; - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiao Yin, Review Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025.
